ai.title: Re-enable mode switching in CLI chat input
ai.summary: Restores agent mode toggle visibility and width calculation in `cli/src/components/chat-input-bar.tsx` and `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-input.ts`. The revert removes temporary disabling logic that forced `estimatedToggleWidth` to 0 and commented out the UI component. This reinstates dynamic width estimation based on `stringWidth` and `isBashMode` state. Scope limited to CLI chat interface components.

eli5.text: When you type in the command-line chat (not bash mode), the agent mode toggle button is visible again in the input bar. The code now correctly calculates the space the toggle takes up based on whether you're in bash mode, so the text input resizes properly. Developers had temporarily hidden the toggle and forced the width calculation to zero, but this change removes that temporary disabling logic and restores the dynamic width estimation that was there before.

ai.title: Opus 4.5 replaces Sonnet in max mode agent orchestration
ai.summary: Anthropic Claude Opus 4.5 replaces Sonnet 4.5 and Gemini in the CLI's max mode orchestration pipeline. The base agent, best-of-n editor implementors/selector, and code reviewer now spawn Opus-specific definitions. This change affects the `.agents` directory and `cli/src/utils/implementor-helpers.ts`, introducing new agent IDs like `code-reviewer-opus` and `editor-implementor-opus` to handle high-complexity coding tasks.

eli5.text: When you ask the command-line tool to work in its highest-powered mode, it now delegates the toughest coding steps to a newer, more capable assistant model instead of the one it used before. If you watch it solve a complex edit, you'll see it quietly hand off planning, editing, and review work to this stronger model running behind the scenes. The older, faster assistant is still used for everyday tasks, so lighter jobs stay quick. Live today for anyone using the max mode.

ai.title: CLI persists agent mode preference
ai.summary: New `cli/src/utils/settings.ts` handles JSON persistence for agent mode, replacing hardcoded `DEFAULT` initialization in `cli/src/state/chat-store.ts`. `loadModePreference` retrieves saved state from `settings.json` in config dir; `saveModePreference` updates it on `setAgentMode` or `toggleAgentMode`. Validation ensures only `DEFAULT`, `MAX`, or `PLAN` persist; invalid or missing values fallback to `DEFAULT`. Scope limited to CLI state management.

eli5.text: When you switch between the normal, max, and plan assistant modes in the CLI, your chosen mode now sticks around after you close and reopen the terminal instead of resetting to the default each time. Behind the scenes, your last-selected mode is saved to a small settings file on your computer, and when the CLI starts up, it reads that file to restore your preference; only the three valid modes are allowed to be saved, and if the file is missing or corrupted, it falls back to the default. The CLI version was bumped at the same time, so this behavior is live today for anyone using the current release.

ai.title: CLI release 1.0.529 ships async tool handlers and Opus 4.5 max mode
ai.summary: Version 1.0.529 in the `cli/release` package.json consolidates four user-visible changes since 1.0.528: agent-runtime tool handlers migrated to async functions returning an `output` object (replacing synchronous returns with a `result` Promise and `State` type), Claude Opus 4.5 replaces Sonnet 4.5 and Gemini in the CLI max mode orchestration pipeline via new agent IDs like `code-reviewer-opus`, the CLI now persists agent mode preference (DEFAULT/MAX/PLAN) in `settings.json`, and mode switching in the CLI chat input is re-enabled with dynamic width estimation restored in `chat-input-bar.tsx` and `use-chat-input.ts`.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in `cli/release/package.json` changes the `version` field from `1.0.528` to `1.0.529`; commit metadata confirms `release-bump` type with analysis notes listing version target and surrounding user-visible updates; no other source files modified.

eli5.text: This release improves how the coding assistant handles tasks behind the scenes and adds support for a more powerful AI model. Tool execution is now faster and more responsive because commands that previously ran synchronously now work asynchronously, so complex operations like search and message handling don't block your workflow. The CLI now remembers which AI mode you prefer (default, max, or plan), so it stops resetting to default every time you restart. The chat input bar brings back the mode toggle, letting you switch between AI tiers smoothly. Max mode now uses Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.5 instead of Sonnet and Gemini, giving you access to a more capable model for difficult coding challenges. Upgrading means a smoother, smarter experience that adapts to your preferences and delivers stronger performance on complex tasks.

ai.title: Copy button adds inline feedback and cursor filtering
ai.summary: Copy button gains inline feedback state and filters cursor characters from clipboard selection. CopyIconButton accepts blocks/content props, extracting text with agent/tool bullets via extractTextFromBlocks. use-clipboard strips CURSOR_CHAR before processing selection. Covers cli/src/components/copy-icon-button.tsx, message-block.tsx, multiline-input.tsx, hooks/use-clipboard.ts.

eli5.text: When you click the copy button on a message, you now see brief confirmation text appear right in place instead of just copying silently. The copied text also strips out the on-screen cursor character that otherwise sometimes gets included in pasted content. This affects any copy button shown on CLI chat message blocks and the multiline input area. It is live today whenever you click a copy action in the CLI.

ai.title: Refactor CLI Message Footer into Component
ai.summary: Extracted footer logic from `message-block.tsx` into new `message-footer.tsx` component. Moves `CopyIconButton`, `ElapsedTimer`, and `FeedbackIconButton` rendering plus associated state hooks. Reduces `MessageBlock` complexity by isolating completion/feedback UI logic.

eli5.text: The row of buttons that appears beneath each assistant reply (copy, timer, and feedback thumbs) has been pulled out of the main message component into its own self-contained building block. This means the main message display no longer has to manage the logic for showing whether a reply is still generating, how long it took, or the thumbs-up/thumbs-down feedback state, so future tweaks to the copy button, elapsed-clock, or feedback controls can be made in one place without touching the larger message-rendering code. Nothing you see or click changes right now the buttons work exactly as before, but the codebase is now cleaner and easier to maintain behind the scenes.

ai.title: Refactor CLI command routing into registry pattern
ai.summary: Extracted CLI command routing logic into a new `command-registry.ts` file, replacing inline handlers in `router.ts`. This introduces a structured `COMMAND_REGISTRY` array defining commands like `/feedback`, `/bash`, and `/login` with their aliases and handler functions. The `routeUserPrompt` function now delegates to `findCommand` from the registry, simplifying the router and improving testability via new unit tests in `router-input.test.ts`. Referral code handling was also moved to a dedicated `referral.ts` module.

eli5.text: When you type a command like /help, /login, or a referral code that starts with ref-, the program now handles it through a clear, organized lookup table instead of a long list of special cases. This makes it easier to see which commands exist, what short forms they accept, and where each one sends you. You won't notice anything different right away unless something previously broke; the change is a behind-the-scenes tidy-up that makes future command-related tweaks safer and easier.

ai.title: Fix stale closure in handlePaste for rapid paste events
ai.summary: Refactor `handlePaste` in `cli/src/components/multiline-input.tsx` to use refs for `value` and `cursorPosition`, preventing stale closure issues during rapid paste events. The handler now reads from `valueRef.current` and `cursorPositionRef.current`, updating refs immediately after each paste to ensure subsequent events see correct state. This change isolates the paste logic from React render cycles, maintaining accurate cursor positioning and text insertion when multiple paste events fire before re-renders.

eli5.text: When you paste text rapidly into the CLI's multiline input, the cursor position and inserted text are now tracked correctly between paste events. The input now uses live references to remember the current text and cursor location, so each new paste sees the updated state instead of a stale snapshot from before the last re-render. If you were pasting multiple blocks in quick succession, the text now lands in the right place without drifting or overwriting. This is live today for all CLI users pasting into the multiline input.

ai.title: Add referrallink to /api/v1/me
ai.summary: GET /api/v1/me now supports `referral_link` as a derived field. `referral_code` added to `User` type and `VALID_USER_INFO_FIELDS` in `web/src/db/user.ts`. Requesting `referral_link` triggers implicit fetch of `referral_code` via `getReferralLink`. Error messages updated to list all valid fields including derived ones.

eli5.text: You can now ask the account API (the /api/v1/me endpoint) to give you back a referral_link, which is a ready-made link that encodes your personal referral_code behind the scenes. The referral_code itself was also added to the list of fields the API recognizes, and if you request referral_link the API quietly pulls your referral_code and builds the link for you via getReferralLink, rather than requiring you to request both pieces separately. The error message for invalid fields was updated so it now lists referral_link (and the other newer fields) as accepted, so it no longer tells you that the new field you just asked for is somehow off-limits.

ai.title: Add /referral command and refactor CLI input mode routing
ai.summary: Added /referral command to CLI to redeem codes or display shareable links, introducing a dedicated `referral` input mode. Refactored chat store from boolean `isBashMode` to string-based `inputMode` ('default', 'bash', 'referral') in `router.ts` and `command-registry.ts` to support multiple input states. Includes new `use-user-details-query` hook for fetching user data and `referral-banner` component for UI display.

eli5.text: The chat tool you use in the terminal now has a new /referral command that lets you redeem a friend's referral code for bonus credits, or type the command with no code to see and copy your own shareable referral link. Behind the scenes, the way the tool handles special input modes switched from a simple yes/no toggle to tracking a named mode (default, bash, or referral), so adding new modes in the future is easier. If you looked, you'd see a small banner appear in referral mode that either shows your link or says it's loading.

ai.title: CLI input modes consolidated into extensible system
ai.summary: Replaced boolean isBashMode with enum inputMode ('default', 'bash', 'referral') in chat-store.ts, driven by new input-modes.ts config registry. chat.tsx and chat-input-bar.tsx now derive UI behavior (suggestions, width, toggle visibility) from getInputModeConfig(mode). Backspace at position 0 exits any special mode, not just bash. Referral mode added with '◎' icon and warning color.

eli5.text: When you're typing a question to the assistant, there's now a new way to switch how the input bar behaves. Instead of a simple on/off toggle for running commands directly, the input bar can be in 'default' mode (normal chat), 'bash' mode (run terminal commands), or 'referral' mode (a new mode with a special icon). The settings for each mode are now defined in one central place, so the look and behavior of the input bar adjust based on which mode is selected. If you press backspace at the start of the input while in bash or referral mode, it exits that mode instead of trying to delete text.

ai.title: CLI elapsed time formatting improves precision
ai.summary: formatElapsedTime now omits zero-value units (e.g. "1m" instead of "1m 0s") and correctly handles sub-minute remainders in the hour range. use-send-message.ts imports and uses this utility for completion time display. Covers cli/src/utils/format-elapsed-time.ts and cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task, the time it took now shows up in a cleaner, more readable way. Instead of always listing every part (like "1m 0s"), it drops the zeros and only shows what's needed (like "1m" or "1h 5m"), and it handles leftover seconds correctly even when hours are involved. If you watch the assistant complete something, the elapsed-time notice below its reply is the only place this matters.

ai.title: CLI input mode refactor, referral error handling
ai.summary: Refactored CLI input mode system to simplify bash mode entry logic and removed unused `isSpecialMode` helper. Added robust error handling and validation for referral code redemption in `router.ts` and `command-registry.ts`, catching exceptions and displaying system messages. Updated `referral-banner.tsx` to handle query errors gracefully. Changed default input placeholder text to lowercase in `input-modes.ts`.

eli5.text: When you're chatting with the assistant and press the exclamation point to switch into bash mode (for running terminal commands), it now switches modes only when you type exactly one exclamation point by itself. Previously, typing just an exclamation point at the start of your message would remove that character and keep the rest of your text intact, which sometimes led to unexpected behavior. Now, pressing the exclamation point by itself cleanly enters bash mode and clears your input, so there's no confusion about what text remains when you start typing your command.

ai.title: CLI referral normalization and user details error handling
ai.summary: Referral code input now normalizes casing and prefixes via `normalizeReferralCode` in `router-utils.ts`. `use-user-details-query.ts` throws errors on API failures instead of returning null. This ensures consistent code handling and explicit failure reporting.

eli5.text: When you type a referral code into the CLI, it now automatically adds the 'ref-' prefix if missing and corrects the casing, so you can type 'ABC123' or 'REF-ABC123' and it will be standardized to 'ref-ABC123' before use. If the system fails to fetch your account details (like your name or subscription info), it will now throw a clear error instead of silently returning nothing. You'll notice fewer confusing mismatches when entering referral codes and clearer error messages if something goes wrong with account-related commands.
